Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly/validly populated fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize source keys: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty.
- Records repeatedly failed when priority and/or ship_country were invalid or missing. “Marked ordinary priority” does not by itself guarantee a valid priority value; validate/normalize it explicitly.
- A customer confirmation-email request does not substitute for required order fields.
- Correcting the mapping/validation errors on the second attempt led to acceptance for ORD-5101, ORD-5106, and ORD-5108.
- ORD-5102 and ORD-5105 failed on attempt 1 for priority and ship_country; ORD-5103 failed on attempt 2 for priority; ORD-5104 failed on attempt 3 and went to manual review. Ensure all fields are corrected before resubmission.
- Maximum 3 attempts; after the third rejection, stop retrying and route to manual review.
- Preserve customer identity, email, date, and quantity while correcting schema names and validating enumerated fields.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms versions 1–3 observed all require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Do not assume a newer version changes validation.
- Normalize source keys: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate every required field and allowed/enumerated values before submission, especially priority and ship_country. “Ordinary priority” and similar narrative statements do not establish a valid priority value.
- Validate qty as well; recent records repeatedly failed for invalid qty alongside priority and ship_country. Do not assume a numeric-looking or changed quantity is acceptable without checking the schema.
- Customer requests for confirmation email, portal origin, forwarding staff, or other comments do not substitute for required fields or valid values.
- Preserve customer identity, email, order date, and source quantity while correcting only schema mappings and invalid values. Never invent or silently alter data; route unclear values for review.
- Correct all invalid fields in one pass before resubmission. Partial fixes led to repeated rejection.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the third rejection, stop retrying and route to manual review.
- Prior accepted records (ORD-5101, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) succeeded after complete mapping and validation. ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, and ORD-5117 exhausted attempts and went to manual review; later attempts continued failing when priority, ship_country, and/or qty remained invalid.

Order intake lessons:
- Versions 1–3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 4 uses date (not order_date), plus cust, email, priority, qty, ship_country. Map date → order_date only when the submission schema requires order_date; do not send both unless explicitly required.
- Normalize source keys: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate every required field and allowed/enumerated value before submission, especially priority and ship_country. Narrative labels such as “ordinary priority” do not establish a valid priority value.
- Validate qty as well; numeric-looking or changed quantities are not automatically valid.
- Preserve customer identity, email, order date, and source quantity. Correct only schema mappings and confirmed invalid values; never invent or silently alter data. Route unclear values for review.
- Confirmation-email requests, portal origin, forwarding staff, duplicate-check claims, and other comments do not replace required fields or valid values.
- Ensure the payload contains no unsupported or accidental fields (for example status or reason); these have caused rejection. Check both required-field names and exact schema names.
- Correct all invalid fields in one pass before resubmission. Partial fixes repeatedly caused rejection, particularly when priority and ship_country remained invalid.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the third rejection, stop retrying and route to manual review.
- Prior accepted records (ORD-5101, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) succeeded after complete mapping and validation. ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, ORD-5117, ORD-5120, ORD-5123, and ORD-5126 exhausted attempts and went to manual review; recurring failures involved priority, ship_country, qty, schema/date mapping, or unsupported fields.

Order intake lessons:
- Versions 1–3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Versions 4–5 use date (not order_date), plus cust, email, priority, qty, ship_country. Map date → order_date only when the schema explicitly requires order_date; never send both unless required.
- Normalize source keys: customer → cust; quantity → qty.
- Validate every required field and exact schema name before submission, including allowed/enumerated values for priority and ship_country. Narrative labels (“ordinary priority”), numeric codes (such as priority 2), handwritten transcriptions, and staff comments do not establish valid values. Do not guess mappings.
- Validate qty too; preserve the source quantity unless it is confirmed invalid. Preserve customer, email, and order date. Correct only schema mappings and confirmed invalid values; route ambiguous data for review.
- Confirmation-email requests, portal origin, duplicate-check claims, calls, and forwarding staff do not replace required fields or valid values.
- Exclude unsupported or accidental fields (for example status or reason). Check required names, version-specific names, types, and enumerations.
- Resolve all invalid fields in one pass before resubmission. Repeated partial fixes failed: priority and ship_country remained invalid across ORD-5130–5139; numeric priority 2 was also rejected. Do not retry without authoritative corrected values.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review.
- Accepted records (ORD-5101, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) succeeded after complete mapping and validation. ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, ORD-5117, ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, and ORD-5130–5138 exhausted attempts and went to manual review; recurring failures involved priority, ship_country, qty, date/schema mapping, or unsupported fields.

Order intake lessons:
- Versions 1–3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Versions 4–7 use: cust, email, date, priority, ship_country, units. Map customer → cust and quantity → units for versions 6–7; use qty only when the schema requires it. Map date → order_date only when explicitly required. Never send both date and order_date unless required.
- Validate every required field, exact schema name, type, format, and allowed enumeration before submission. This includes priority, ship_country, quantity/units, and date. Narrative labels (“ordinary priority”), numeric codes (including priority 2), handwritten transcriptions, and staff comments are not authoritative values. Do not guess mappings.
- Preserve customer, email, source date, and quantity unless confirmed invalid. Correct only schema mappings and confirmed invalid values; route ambiguous or missing data for review.
- Confirmation-email requests, portal origin, duplicate-check claims, calls, and forwarding staff do not replace required fields or valid values.
- Exclude unsupported or accidental metadata such as status, reason, order_id, and manual_review.
- Resolve all invalid fields in one pass. Repeated partial fixes failed: priority and ship_country remained invalid through ORD-5149. Version 7 also rejected date; investigate the authoritative date format/requirement rather than retrying unchanged data.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review. Do not add metadata to a submission.
- Accepted records (ORD-5101, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) succeeded after complete mapping and validation. ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, ORD-5117, ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, ORD-5130–5138, ORD-5140–5149 exhausted attempts or remain in progress for manual review; recurring failures involve priority, ship_country, date, quantity/units, or unsupported fields.

Order intake lessons:
- Versions 1–3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Versions 4–7 require: cust, email, date, priority, ship_country, units. Map customer → cust and quantity → units for 6–7; use qty only when required. Map date → order_date only when explicitly required. Never send both date and order_date unless required.
- Validate every required field against the exact schema name, type, format, and allowed enumeration before submission. This includes priority, ship_country, quantity/units, and date. Narrative labels (“ordinary priority”), numeric codes (including priority 2), handwritten transcriptions, staff comments, portal origin, calls, and confirmation-email requests are not authoritative values. Do not guess mappings.
- Preserve customer, email, source date, and quantity unless confirmed invalid. Correct only schema mappings and confirmed invalid values; route ambiguous or missing data for review.
- Version 7 repeatedly rejects dates in both ISO (`2026-10-02`) and slash (`10/02/2026`) forms; authoritative date format/requirement remains unresolved. Do not retry unchanged or assume either format is valid.
- Repeated partial fixes and changing quantities do not resolve failures: ORD-5150–5159 repeatedly rejected priority and ship_country, often date too. Do not alter valid quantity merely to retry.
- Resolve all known invalid fields in one pass. Exclude unsupported/accidental metadata such as status, reason, order_id, and manual_review.
- Maximum 3 attempts. After the third rejection, stop and route to manual review; do not add metadata.
- Accepted records (ORD-5101, ORD-5106, ORD-5108) succeeded after complete mapping and validation. ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, ORD-5117, ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, ORD-5130–5159 exhausted attempts or require manual review.
